summary: Intermittent RBAC denial on Analytics Portal after Okta profile events; identity event consumer lag + cache TTL interaction
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-05 09:20 UTC multiple internal users reported 403 / "role not found" errors when accessing the Analytics Portal. Failures correlated with recent Okta group membership changes made by HR/IT provisioning. Impact: ~30 engineers intermittently unable to open dashboards or run queries for ~30-90 minutes. Not a full outage but blocked several oncall and reporting workflows.

Observed behavior: Users re-authenticating sometimes succeeded immediately; other times they needed support to trigger a manual RBAC cache invalidation. Errors surfaced as 403s from analytics-portal with response body: "RBAC: user has no roles for resource".

Environment details: Production (us-east). Identity pipeline: Okta -> event-stream (kafka) -> identity-events-consumer -> identity-service (applies changes) -> rbac-cache (in-memory cache in identity-service with 5m TTL) -> service-side authorization checks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Make an Okta group membership change for a test user (add to analytics_readers).
2) Wait for the provisioning change to be emitted to the Okta event stream (Okta system->event webhook).
3) Observe identity-events-consumer processing lag in metrics (consumer lag > 0).
4) Immediately attempt to access Analytics Portal while consumer lag exists and rbac-cache TTL has not expired — expected: 403 despite user being in Okta group.
5) After either the event consumer catches up OR cache TTL expires (5m) and cache invalidation occurs, access is restored.
logs_snippets: 2026-03-05T09:22:11Z identity-events-consumer [WARN] partition 3 lag=1248 events; processing stalled
2026-03-05T09:24:09Z analytics-portal [INFO] authz deny user=apatel reason=RBAC_CACHE_MISS ttl=240s
comments: 2026-03-05 09:30 UTC — Support (Marco Ruiz): Confirmed multiple 403 reports. Asked affected users to capture screenshots and exact timestamps. Asked oncall SRE to check consumer lag and identity-service logs.

2026-03-05 09:42 UTC — SRE Oncall (Diego Morales): Observed kafka consumer lag spike on topic okta.events.consumer-group (partition 2/3). Consumer CPU at 95% on identity-events-consumer-1; replicas were restarted during a deploy window 09:10-09:15 UTC. Possible backlog created by mid-deploy transient. Increased consumer parallelism from 2->4 to catch up; lag dropped to zero by 09:58.

2026-03-05 10:05 UTC — Identity Eng (Lina Chen): Noted cache TTL interaction: identity-service caches role mappings for 5m; when events were delayed, newly-added Okta memberships were not reflected until either consumer processed or cache expired. Working hypothesis: cache TTL too long for high-change groups + delayed event processing leads to transient denies. Added temporary endpoint to invalidate rbac-cache per-user/org. Cleared cache for affected users which restored access.
2026-03-05 12:10 UTC — Support (Marco Ruiz): Customers (internal) confirmed access restored. Documented mitigation steps and asked Identity Eng to propose a long-term fix.

2026-03-07 15:20 UTC — Identity Eng (Lina Chen): Implemented hotfix: rbac-cache now subscribes to an internal event invalidation topic. As part of the fix we publish an invalidation event after successful processing of Okta membership events. Also increased consumer autoscaling threshold to spawn additional pods when lag > 500. Deployed to prod 15:05 UTC with smoke tests passing.

2026-03-08 09:00 UTC — Postmortem (Aisha Patel): Verified monitoring alarms and added runbook steps: when consumer lag > 600 for >5m, escalate to SRE to increase parallelism and optionally trigger manual invalidations. Closing ticket after monitoring validated for 48h.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: sequence of events — a deploy/restart window at 09:10 caused identity-events-consumer to fall behind; meanwhile HR bulk group changes were processed causing many membership events to be queued. Because identity-service relies on a TTL'd in-memory RBAC cache (5m), the processed events were not applied to cached entries until cache expired or explicit invalidation occurred -> transient denies. Root cause contributors: (1) small consumer parallelism and CPU saturation during deploy, (2) RBAC cache TTL too long for high-churn groups, (3) no immediate cache invalidation on event processing success. Metrics reviewed: consumer lag timeline, identity-service cache hit ratio, analytics-portal 403 spike. No database corruption or Okta webhook failures found.
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigation: increased consumer parallelism to drain the backlog; provided support workaround to invalidate per-user RBAC cache via admin endpoint; manually cleared cache for affected users.

Long-term fix (deployed 2026-03-07): publish explicit cache-invalidation events after identity-events-consumer successfully applies membership changes; adjust auto-scaling for identity-events-consumer to react at lag > 500; reduce RBAC cache TTL for high-churn groups from 5m -> 60s and keep default 5m for low-churn groups. Added dashboards: consumer lag, cache-miss ratio per org, and a synthetic auth check for analytics-portal for critical service accounts.

Follow-ups: (1) Add documented runbook section (Confluence) for consumer-lag incidents and manual cache invalidation steps. (2) Evaluate persistent storage for role mappings to allow immediate lookups rather than in-memory TTL dependency.
